title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-marcus
notes:
Summary:
- Personal scratchpad from investigating the regional failover + smart-routing fallback issue that started 2026-02-27 ~09:12 PST. Symptoms: a subset of customer traffic (eu-west customers) saw 504s and 'no healthy upstream' errors for ~18 minutes as router layer attempted fallback to cheaper pool; fallback policy mis-evaluated and routed to a drained pool in us-west causing connection refused.

Timeline (local times):
- 09:12: incoming spike from eu-west -> observed increase in p50/p95 latency in eu-west router nodes (kibana query: service:router AND region:eu-west AND response_code:5xx)
- 09:14: first 504s reported by customer telemetry (request-id examples: req-0a7f3c, req-0a7f8d)
- 09:17: automated fallback triggered (policy: cost-first, allow_cross_region:true, max_latency_ms:400). Router logged fallback decision but health-check for target pool returned stale status.
- 09:28: manual mitigation: coordinate with SRE to drain failing router and re-route traffic to eu-west-hot pool. Restarted router pods in eu-west; full recovery by 09:30.

Commands I ran (notes / outputs):
- kubectl (on prod cluster, context=redwood-prod-eu):
  - kubectl get pods -n serving-runtime -l app=router -o wide
  - kubectl logs -n serving-runtime router-eu-7f8d -c router --since=30m | grep "fallback" | tail -50
    -> saw repeated: "WARN fallback: selected pool eu-cost-01 but health_check=UNKNOWN (last_ok=2026-02-27T08:50:12Z)"
  - kubectl exec -n serving-runtime router-eu-7f8d -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9100/healthz
    -> returned 200 OK for local process

- Redis / config store checks (policy store on config-db-prod):
  - redis-cli -h config-db-prod GET fallback:policy:eu-west:customer:acme -> returned JSON string (policy_version: 3, prefer_cost:true, cross_region_allowed:true)
  - redis-cli TTL fallback:policy:eu-west:customer:acme -> 0 (no expiry)

- LB / networking checks:
  - curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: req-0a7f3c" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> saw 504 and upstream reset in tcpdump logs
  - kubectl exec -n infra-tooling lb-check -- curl -v http://eu-cost-01.internal:8080/health -> connection refused (immediately)

Error snippets observed in router logs:
- "ERROR router: failed to connect to backend eu-cost-01: dial tcp 10.42.15.98:8080: connect: connection refused"
- "WARN fallback: selected pool eu-cost-01 but health_check=UNKNOWN (last_ok=2026-02-27T08:50:12Z)"
- "ERROR policy-eval: KeyError: 'policy_version' (while evaluating policy for customer=acme)"
- Upstream errors from model-serv: "504 upstream timeout after 29s"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stale health-state + aggressive fallback policy: Health check machinery returned UNKNOWN for eu-cost-01 but policy eval allowed selection of pools with UNKNOWN health when cross_region_allowed=true. Race: health check flapped due to temporary node restart, but cache TTL for health status was long (10m), so router used stale status and attempted connection.
2) Config race during policy rollout: A policy schema change (policy_version bump) was rolled out 2026-02-27 08:45; some routers had mixed schema (old code expecting policy_version field). KeyError seen suggests partial rollout left some routers reading slightly different payloads leading to incorrect fallback evaluation.
3) Network partition / firewall rule misconfiguration between eu routers and eu-cost pool nodes (iptables or cloud provider ephemeral network issue). Evidence: connection refused from pod IP at same time.
4) Over-eager cross-region fallback: cost-first policy allowed cross-region fallback to us-west cost pool; those nodes were near capacity and refused connections.

Reproduction steps (best-effort):
1) Simulate health flap: on eu-cost-01 pool node, restart model-server container, ensure health-check endpoint returns 500 for ~2 minutes.
2) Trigger policy eval: send sample inference traffic with header X-Dev-Test: routing-fallback and watch router logs for 'selected pool' messages.
3) Run local policy-eval tool (scripts/policy_eval.py) with the customer policy payload retrieved from config-db-prod to confirm behavior under missing 'policy_version'.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Temporarily disabled cross_region_allowed for cost-first policies for affected customers (redis write: fallback:policy:eu-west:customer:acme -> set prefer_cost:false) at 09:20 to reduce cross-region failovers.
- Restarted router pods in eu-west (kubectl rollout restart deploy/router-eu) to pick up consistent config and clear transient KeyError states.
- Manually re-routed traffic to eu-west-hot pool until eu-cost nodes healed.

Follow-ups / action items (TODOs):
- CONFIG: add required schema validation for fallback policy payloads at read time (reject/migrate records missing policy_version). Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-03-05.
- HEALTH: reduce health-state TTL from 10m -> 30s for router cache or implement immediate re-check if policy eval would select UNKNOWN nodes. Owner: Marcus. Due: 2026-03-02.
- OBSERVABILITY: add metric for 'fallback_selected_unhealthy' and alert when >5/min. Also alert on KeyError in policy-eval. Owner: Olivia. Due: 2026-03-03.
- RUNTIME: change fallback policy thresholds: require healthy=true (not UNKNOWN) unless forced by emergency_override flag. Document rollout plan. Owner: Eng Platform. Due: 2026-03-10.
- TESTING: add integration test that simulates health-flap during policy rollout and validates safe fallback behavior. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-03-12.

Notes / loose thoughts:
- The KeyError suggests the policy rollout was not backward compatible. Need a small migration utility that backfills policy_version for existing policies before turning on strict validation.
- Consider adding a 'last_seen_ok' metadata check and require last_seen_ok within X seconds for pools to be eligible for fallback.
- For high-signal customers (SLA), prefer 'latency-first' or 'local-only' profiles to avoid cross-region exposure by default.
- Add a documented postmortem template link to CONFLUENCE-SS-2341 and copy final investigation notes here.

Raw log excerpts (sanitized):
[2026-02-27T09:15:22Z] router-eu-7f8d WARN fallback: customer=acme selected=eu-cost-01 health=UNKNOWN last_ok=2026-02-27T08:50:12Z
[2026-02-27T09:15:23Z] router-eu-7f8d ERROR connect: dial tcp 10.42.15.98:8080: connect: connection refused request_id=req-0a7f3c
[2026-02-27T09:17:05Z] policy-eval ERROR KeyError: 'policy_version' customer=acme stack=policy_eval.py:87

If anything is missing / want me to expand specific sections (more command outputs, kibana queries, full log tails), I can paste them here. This is a working note; will convert to a concise postmortem once follow-ups are assigned and we've validated fixes.
